He offers them his chair; Sylvie kills him, the timelines branch beyond counting, and Loki is dumped in a TVA that no longer knows him, under a statue of Kang. Season two is Loki unstuck in time and the loom that cannot hold the branches, ending with him understanding what the job actually costs: he climbs to the end of time, takes the branches in his hands, and holds the multiverse together himself - a god on a throne, alone, choosing it, which is the opposite of everything he wanted at the start.

Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, facing impeachment for an illegal super-soldier programme, sends her deniable assets to kill each other and burn the evidence: Yelena Belova, John Walker, Ghost and Taskmaster all arrive at the same vault expecting a different job. Taskmaster is killed in the first minutes. The survivors, plus Bob - a confused man in a hospital gown found in the vault - fight their way out, collect Alexei and Bucky Barnes on the way, and work out that Bob is the programme: Sentry, the only successful subject, with the power of a sun and a lifetime of depression and addiction underneath it.

Valentina presents Bob as her new Avenger, and he comes apart. His shadow self, the Void, spreads across Manhattan turning everyone it touches into a memory of their worst moment. There is no way to punch it. Yelena walks into the dark after him and into the shame he is trapped in - the childhood room he cannot leave - and the rest of the team follow her in one by one and simply stay with him until he can come back. The team, badly suited to the job and known to be, are rebranded by Valentina as the New Avengers in front of the world's press.
thunderbolts.stinger: Fourteen months on, the team hold the Avengers name and tower - and a ship bearing the Fantastic Four's insignia comes through a portal above them.

paragraphs: Shaun parks cars in San Francisco with his friend Katy and has told her nothing true about himself. He is Shang-Chi, son of Xu Wenwu, who found the ten rings a thousand years ago, has ruled a criminal empire ever since, and trained his son from the age of seven to be an assassin. Attacked on a bus for the pendant his mother left him, Shang-Chi goes to Macau for his sister Xialing, who was refused that training and built her own fighting ring instead, and both are taken by their father.

Wenwu is hearing his dead wife's voice calling from behind the gate of her home village, Ta Lo, and intends to break it open; the voice is the Dweller-in-Darkness, a soul-eating creature imprisoned there. The family reach Ta Lo, are taught by their aunt Ying Nan and fight alongside its people and its dragon; Wenwu, realising too late, gives Shang-Chi the rings as he dies. Shang-Chi kills the Dweller with the Great Protector's help, and comes back to San Francisco to be dragged straight out of a restaurant by Wong for a meeting with Banner and Captain Marvel about what the rings actually are.
shang-chi.stinger: The rings are a beacon, sending a signal to something far away; Xialing takes over her father's organisation rather than dissolving it.

paragraphs: An animated anthology about the Hatut Zeraze, Wakanda's War Dogs, sent across centuries to recover vibranium artefacts that left the country. Each episode is a self-contained historical story with a different agent: Bronze Age Aegea and a stolen relic among Greek warriors, a mission in Han-era China, a first-century pursuit, and a fifteenth-century voyage, with the recurring thread of what the recovery of these objects costs the agents and the people they meet.

The agents rarely come home clean. An artefact is recovered and someone who trusted its holder pays for it; an operative who spends years abroad has to decide whether the mission or the people she has come to know matter more; and in every era the same order comes down from home, which is to take the vibranium back and leave no trace of Wakanda behind.

It deepens Wakanda's history rather than advancing any current plot - how the isolation was enforced, who did the enforcing, and the long argument inside the country about whether hiding is protection or abdication. Nothing in it is required to follow the Black Panther films, and no character from them appears.

Agatha Harkness is still trapped in the persona Wanda left her in, playing a murder-detective in Westview, until a young man breaks the spell. Powerless and hunted, she is persuaded to walk the Witches' Road - a trial that grants a witch what she most wants at the end of it - and assembles a coven for it: Lilia the divination witch, Jennifer Kale the potions witch, Alice Wu-Gulliver, whose family is under a curse, the fraud Sharon Davis, and the sigil-bound teenager who calls himself Teen and cannot say his own name.

Each trial kills someone, and Agatha's history of draining witches for power is the real danger the coven walks with. The Road turns out not to exist: Agatha invented the legend centuries ago as a way to lure and kill covens, and this one she and Teen conjured together. Teen is Billy Maximoff, Wanda's son, whose consciousness landed in a dying boy's body; Agatha's own son Nicholas was taken by Death, which is Rio Vidal, the woman she has loved and fled from for three hundred years. Agatha gives herself to Rio to save Billy, and stays with him afterwards as a ghost while he goes looking for his brother.

A year after Foggy Nelson is murdered in front of him by Bullseye, Matt Murdock has hung up the suit and practises law with Kirsten McDuffie, while Wilson Fisk - also out of the life, he says - runs for mayor of New York and wins. The season is the two of them circling each other in daylight, each insisting they have changed, with Murdock defending a vigilante called White Tiger and Fisk building an anti-vigilante task force out of the police officers who already ran one.

Fisk's marriage, his therapist, and a serial killer subplot pull at the seams, and Murdock's restraint fails in stages. By the finale Fisk has declared martial law over the city, arrested his opponents, and made the mask illegal; Murdock puts the suit back on to fight it, and the show ends with New York under an occupation and a resistance forming around him. Karen Page, Frank Castle and Maya Lopez all pass through it.

On a retro-futurist Earth of its own, four astronauts changed by cosmic radiation four years ago are the planet's beloved public scientists: Reed Richards, who stretches; Sue Storm, who turns invisible and throws force fields; Johnny Storm, who ignites; and Ben Grimm, permanently rocky. Sue is pregnant, and the family's ordinary anxiety about that is the film's spine. Then the Silver Surfer arrives to announce the world has been marked for consumption by Galactus.

Reed's plan is to reason with a god and fails; Galactus offers a bargain instead, because Sue's unborn child carries power he wants for himself. The family refuse in public, and the world - which adored them - turns on them for it. Franklin is born in space during the escape. The end is a rescue rather than a duel: the Surfer breaks with Galactus after seeing what he is being asked to take, the family lure Galactus into a teleport bridge, and Sue burns herself out pushing him through it. Franklin's power brings her back. The four raise the child in a city that has to work out how to be grateful again.

Scott Lang has written a memoir and is enjoying being liked. His daughter Cassie, now a teenager and an activist, has built a device to signal into the quantum realm - which pulls the entire family, plus Hank and Janet, down into it. Janet, who spent thirty years there and has told nobody why, knows exactly what is waiting: Kang the Conqueror, a variant exiled there by his own kind, whom she once helped repair his ship before realising what he would do with it, and then sabotaged.

The realm has cities, rebels and a resistance, and Kang has been conquering it while he waits. He blackmails Lang into stealing his power core back by threatening Cassie; Lang and Hope multiply themselves into a swarm of variants to get it, and Kang is destroyed in his own engine after Lang refuses him. The family get home. The film's function is to establish Kang as the franchise's next threat, and it closes on a council of thousands of his variants agreeing that the exile's death is the provocation they were waiting for.
ant-man-and-the-wasp-quantumania.stinger: Loki and Mobius watch a Victorian-era variant, Victor Timely, lecture a crowd.

paragraphs: Three Fox-era films grouped as one entry, because they are the ones Deadpool & Wolverine assumes you have seen. Deadpool (2016): Wade Wilson, a mercenary with terminal cancer, takes an experimental cure from Ajax that tortures a mutation out of him, leaving him unkillable and disfigured; he spends the film hunting Ajax to fix his face, gets Vanessa back, kills him anyway, and narrates the whole thing to the audience.

Deadpool 2 (2018): Vanessa is murdered in the opening, and Wade's attempt to die fails. Cable comes back from the future to kill a teenage mutant, Russell, before he grows into the man who burns Cable's family; Wade assembles X-Force, loses all of them in a parachute drop except Domino, and finally saves Russell by taking a bullet for him with a power-suppressing collar on. Cable spends his one trip home to bring Wade back.

Logan (2017): in 2029 mutants are nearly extinct, Logan is dying of adamantium poisoning and driving a limousine, and Charles Xavier is hidden in Mexico with a degenerative brain condition that causes seizures lethal to everyone near him. Logan is dragged into escorting Laura - X-23, a girl grown from his genetic material - to a refuge in North Dakota, pursued by Transigen. Xavier is killed, Logan kills the corporate clone made from him, and dies in the woods with Laura calling him Daddy; she turns his grave cross on its side to make an X.

Three Fox X-Men films grouped as the background the animated series and Deadpool & Wolverine draw on. X-Men (2000): Rogue and Wolverine are taken in by Xavier's school, and Magneto - a Holocaust survivor who believes coexistence is impossible - tries to force mutation on the world's leaders with a machine powered by Rogue, which would have killed them all. X2 (2003): Colonel William Stryker, who made Wolverine what he is, attacks the mansion and turns a captured Xavier's mind into a weapon aimed at every mutant alive; the X-Men and Magneto work together to stop it, and Jean Grey drowns holding back a flood to save the team.

Days of Future Past (2014): in a future where Sentinels have exterminated mutants and most of humanity, the survivors send Wolverine's consciousness back to 1973 to stop Mystique assassinating Bolivar Trask - the act that convinced the world to build them. He has to reconcile a broken young Xavier and an imprisoned Magneto to do it. Mystique chooses not to kill Trask, on camera, and the timeline rewrites: the dead are alive again, and the future the film opened on never happens.

Wade Wilson has quit and sells used cars, until the TVA pulls him in and explains that his universe is dying: its anchor being, Logan, is dead, and the timeline is being allowed to decay. Offered a place in the Sacred Timeline and refused a way to save his friends, Wade goes looking for a replacement Wolverine across the multiverse and comes back with the worst one - a drunk who got his whole world killed. The TVA agent Paradox, meanwhile, is quietly building a time ripper to destroy the universe faster and take the credit.

Both are dumped in the Void, the junkyard at the end of time, ruled by Charles Xavier's twin Cassandra Nova. There they find the discarded heroes of the Fox era - Elektra, Blade, Gambit, X-23 - who join a doomed charge against Cassandra's forces. Wade and Logan take the ripper's two ends together, which should kill them both, and survive because there are two of them. Deadpool's universe is saved and Logan stays in it, walking into the bar where Wade's friends are waiting.
